citation: [The 2100 block of Prairie Avenue looking north-west, early 1890s.] Street photograph; photographer not named. Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'Moving house on Prairie Avenue, 1891', The Story of a House (blog), August 2014, which names the houses left to right as Max Rothschild (2112), Harriet Rees (2110), Mark Kimball (2108), John B. Sherman (2100) and Ebenezer Buckingham (2036).
author: unknown photographer
repository: Glessner House Museum blog 'The Story of a House'; the original holder is not credited. Prairie library image a20-glessner-2100-block-west-side-1890s, its rights recorded there as unknown, link only; the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a20-glessner-2100-block-west-side-1890s.jpg).
locator: The roadway's edges: at the left edge, two posts before 2112's stoop and one at the curb before 2110 (x 330-360 of 900); at the right edge, the east curb with a row of round-topped posts.
rights_note: The reproduction carries no rights statement and names no holder. Only forms, counts and places are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-27 (T-3198) from the image store's copy, 900 x 318 px sepia. The camera stands in the roadway near 2114-2120 looking north-north-west.
note: The one picture of the 2100 block's curbs. Round, white, domed stone posts about knee to hip high stand at the curb: a pair at the picture's left edge before 2112, one before 2110, and a row of five or more along the east curb at the picture's right edge. None shows before 2108 or 2100 at that distance, though the trees could hide one. The posts differ in height and in their domes; none carries a ring or a step.
what_it_supplies: carriage posts at the west side before 2112 and 2110, round with domed tops
a row of the same posts along the east curb opposite
a gas lamp on a post at the west curb further north
what_it_does_not_supply: the posts' sizes: no measure stands beside them
which east-side houses the row stands before: the picture's edge cuts them off
colour or stone: the photograph is sepia
